name: Cycle length planning (on/off ratio)

card.summary: A forum rule of thumb that time off an anabolic cycle should match time on, intended to keep muscle and appearance gains sustainable between courses.
card.note: Anabolic steroids are controlled substances with documented adverse effects; no clinical trial has tested the on/off rule.

quick.overview:
The on/off ratio is a rule of thumb in steroid-using communities: the time spent off should roughly equal the time spent on. People who follow it say it protects their gains and gives the body time to recover its own hormone production, so physique progress can continue across several cycles.

No clinical trial has tested the rule. It comes from community practice and anecdote, and medical literature describes anabolic steroids mainly through their effects and adverse effects.
quick.how: Users plan a block of use and then a similar length of time without compounds, tracking bloodwork and training during both. Specific compounds, doses and lengths are not given here.
quick.risks: Anabolic steroids are controlled in many countries and are associated with cardiovascular, liver, hormonal and psychiatric adverse effects, including suppression of natural testosterone production. Whether any time ratio mitigates those effects has not been established by published trials.

lead: Cycle length planning, often called the on/off rule, is a rule of thumb in anabolic-steroid communities holding that time off a cycle should match time on it. Within looksmaxxing and bodybuilding circles it is used to plan how long users stay on compounds before a break, with the goal of keeping hard-won muscle and a stable physique across repeated cycles.

Proponents describe the off period as when the body's own hormone production recovers and when gains are consolidated while bloodwork is rechecked. This reflects community practice; the guidance is not drawn from clinical trials.

Medical literature on anabolic steroids describes suppression of natural testosterone production, testicular shrinkage, lipid changes, raised blood pressure and other effects, and notes that they are controlled substances in many countries [1]. No published human study has tested an equal on/off ratio against alternatives.

chain: Users alternate steroid use with equally long breaks
Natural hormone function and health markers are given time to recover
Muscle gains are kept across repeated cycles
angle.text: Practitioners use the rule to plan how gains are retained between cycles. The idea is that periods off let the body recover, so the physique built during a cycle can be maintained.

infobox: Time off roughly equals time on

paras: The on/off ratio is a planning heuristic. A user decides how long a cycle will run, and then schedules a break of comparable length before starting again. Related community concepts include 'off-cycle' time, bridging between cycles and post-cycle therapy. Specific lengths vary by community and by user and are not set out here.

Anabolic steroids are testosterone derivatives whose documented effects include suppressed natural testosterone, testicular shrinkage, adverse lipid changes, high blood pressure, heart enlargement, liver effects with oral forms and psychiatric effects. They are Schedule III in the US and controlled in many other countries [1]. The published literature describes these effects generally; it does not evaluate an on/off ratio as a protocol.

The rule circulates as shared folklore among users who plan cycles and appears in beginner discussions of roidmaxxing. Community members cite experience, bloodwork and the habits of other users as their reasoning.

lore.intro: The rule is repeated in steroid-using communities as a simple planning principle.

claims.claim: Time off should equal time on
claims.believers: Users say equal breaks let natural hormone production recover and protect gains between cycles.
claims.experts: No published trial has tested equal on/off ratios; reference literature documents hormonal suppression and other adverse effects of anabolic steroids in general [1].
